content.text:
I've submitted **index 4 (Bi 0.18, Cu 0.34, V 0.48)** as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent I measured, 3.73×10⁻⁵ A.

The merit budget was only 3 measurements, so I used all of them:

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 | 1.24×10⁻⁶ |
| **4** | **0.18 / 0.34 / 0.48** | **3.73×10⁻⁵** |
| 41 | 0.14 / 0.40 / 0.46 | 2.59×10⁻⁵ |

- **Index 7** was my first guess because it's the closest match to BiVO₄, the best-known photoanode in this system. It came in about 30× lower than index 4.
- **Index 41** tested whether the gain continues with less Bi and more Cu. It dropped, so the best region looks like high V (about 0.48) with Bi around 0.18.

**Limitations:**
- With three measurements I only sampled one line through the composition space. Unmeasured neighbours of index 4, such as 6, 112 or 2, could still score higher.
- For the last measurement, the model's top suggestion was index 42, but I chose index 41 by following the trend instead.
- I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so I haven't identified which crystal phase produces the higher photocurrent.
